notes: s014/s015 split the supplied relative clause across the article and its expressed head noun, giving that which to τά and only is lacking to ὑστερήματα on rule 22. Rule 22 is scoped to a substantival article, and rule 31's test — whether the article governs an expressed head noun — makes this one attributive, ὑστερήματα being expressed. Rule 92 is the governing rule for an expressed noun the ASV recasts as a finite relative clause: the noun carries the supplied relativizer and copula together and the article keeps only the determiner or antecedent pronoun the ASV writes, as τοὺς … ἀποστόλους → them that were at GAL.1.17 does. The unit had already placed the copula on the noun under rule 53, so the relativizer was stranded on the article against its own analysis. Only these two units change; the unit count stays at 18.
